facts.text: Star Danielle Fishel said the cast spent four weeks of 14-to-18-hour days surrounded by neon green paint. Nearly the whole movie was shot on a green stage.
Screenwriters Patrick Casey and Worm Miller later wrote the Sonic the Hedgehog movies and Violent Night. Before that, they wrote Gamebox 1.0 and both Dorm Daze comedies.
Gamebox 1.0 was directed by brothers David and Scott Hillenbrand, who also made the 1999 giant-snake movie King Cobra.
The Hillenbrand brothers' previous film, National Lampoon Presents Dorm Daze (2003), grossed just $436,365 worldwide and holds a 0% Rotten Tomatoes score from seven critics.
Danielle Fishel plays two roles: Kate, the murdered girlfriend, and Princess, the video-game version of her. Fishel said Kate gave her a break so she could 'use my face again.'
The game worlds borrow freely: the crime level copies Grand Theft Auto, and later scenes echo the cabin from The Evil Dead, the foggy woods of Resident Evil and the look of Silent Hill.
Fishel said game-world Princess wore heavy makeup, so 'in person you look like a complete freak.' She added that video game characters have few expressions, so she put all her emotion into her eyes.
DVD Talk compared the film to Tron, The Matrix and Brainscan. Star Danielle Fishel also told the Daily Bruin she'd recommend it to anyone who liked Tron.
The film won Best Screenplay and Best Visual Effects at the Horror and Fantasy Film Festival in Malaga, Spain, according to a 2007 Daily Bruin piece.
The DVD cover used a Saw-style design, but DVD Talk's Scott Weinberg stressed that Gamebox 1.0 is 'definitely not a horror movie.' It's rated PG-13.
Danielle Fishel said she grew up playing Nintendo and always wanted to be a video game princess. Gamebox 1.0 was her third movie with the Hillenbrand brothers.
Star Nate Richert is also a musician. He released an album, Tone Control, in 2004, the same year this movie premiered. He plays guitar, banjo, drums and harmonica.
Two TGIF sitcom alumni lead this film. Nate Richert played Harvey on Sabrina the Teenage Witch, and Danielle Fishel played Topanga on Boy Meets World.
Songwriters Ali Dee and Zach Danziger wrote tracks credited to at least five different acts on the soundtrack, including Basko, Invisible Man, Boomish, The Skeem and The Grand Skeem.
Fishel shot this alongside the National Lampoon's Dorm Daze movies. She said those shoots also ran 16 to 18 hours a day, over about three weeks to a month.
Danielle Fishel believes the Hillenbrand brothers hired her and Nate Richert partly because they'd worked together before and were reliable, which matters on a grueling green-screen shoot.
Mariana Klaveno made her screen debut in this movie. She later became known for TV vampire roles.
DVD Talk said some effects here are 'appreciably slick' and others 'purely amateur hour,' and that the film would need 'at least 10 million bucks' to reach its potential.
Scott Weinberg of DVD Talk said the film is too choppy and 'a little too beholden to other movies.' He still gave it 3 out of 5 as a rental for game fans.
Before acting, Patrick Kilpatrick (villain Ronald Hobbes) worked as a bodyguard for Jimi Hendrix, Pink Floyd, the Grateful Dead and the Beach Boys when they toured New York in the 1970s.
The movie's three game levels are Crime Spree, Zombie Land and Alien Planet. Its influences include Videodrome, eXistenZ and Gremlins, which it references.
Danielle Fishel said the movie's message is about escaping reality: 'You can't just drown yourself in a video game.'
Rick Bentley of The Fresno Bee gave it a D+, writing: 'There are only two words to describe the lousy graphics, bad acting and stupid story in Gamebox 1.0: game over.'
The soundtrack leans on indie acts such as Ghost In The Machine, Boomish, Freakhouse and Maple Mars.
The Hillenbrand brothers later directed Transylmania, which opened on 1,007 screens with $263,941, then the worst opening ever for a film in over 1,000 theaters.
Patrick Kilpatrick plays Ronald Hobbes. He also played a villain in Eraser and Death Warrant, and he was in Minority Report.
In 2012 financial backers sued the Hillenbrand brothers. Their company countersued, alleging fraud and seeking at least $107 million, per Wikipedia's Transylmania article.
The film shot in 2004 but reached U.S. DVD only on April 10, 2007, from Lionsgate. Fishel said it had been filmed about three years earlier.
Patrick Cavanaugh, who plays Peter here, later appeared on Mad Men and Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.
Tomb Raider, 2001: A Space Odyssey, and the games Halo: Combat Evolved and Mario Kart: Super Circuit are all referenced or shown in this movie.
Danielle Fishel was first cast as a one-episode guest on the Boy Meets World pilot. When the actress playing Topanga wasn't working out, Fishel read on the spot and won the role.
Nate Richert played Harvey Kinkle in 123 episodes of Sabrina the Teenage Witch (1996 to 2003), and made a brief TV return in Home Work in 2020.
